scope.purpose: Shared invented examples for later host and engine implementations; not a runner, implementation PASS, deployment instruction or owner approval.

interpretation.fixture_metadata_is_not_protocol: Only request, expect.response and explicit host_translation_example objects in browser steps are protocol messages. arrange, durable assertions, clocks, I/O counters, setup records and trusted_content_import raw-input/outcome assertions are harness metadata. Trusted import has no invented BrowserOp or public response shape.
interpretation.independence: Reset to common synthetic setup before EACH scenario. Steps inside a scenario are sequential unless a barrier explicitly orders contenders. No dependence across scenarios/cases.
interpretation.ids: All 32-hex identities are invented SHA-256-prefix fixture labels. Adapter may deterministically allocate these IDs or bind its allocated IDs bijectively; the same identity must compare equal through replay/recovery. Contract SHA is the only production-derived hash in this fixture.
interpretation.opaque_hashes: Hashes labeled invented attestations stand for trusted fake-producer assertions. Artifact/text/profile hashes that bind explicit bytes are computed. No invented digest or approval authenticates a real import, actor or print.
interpretation.time: Default synthetic clock is common_setup.clock (2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z). Every scenario declares its initial clock and every step declares its clock. Apply that step clock before its request; clocks never decrease within a scenario. Replay/read/recovery return older stored timestamps unchanged. New reviews use the step clock and expire exactly five minutes later; status validity is sixty seconds. No wall-clock waiting occurs.
interpretation.transport: Replace every device transport, DNS and discovery dependency with in-memory fakes. Device IDs receipt-fx-* belong only to the fake registry; no live endpoints are present. Unexpected real I/O is a test failure before any access.
interpretation.payloads: FIXTURE-OPAQUE-PAYLOAD blobs are injected frozen artifacts for transport/state tests, not ESC/POS renderer golden files. Actual renderer profile tests stay separate. An exact-retry case must copy its explicit parent bytes without rendering.
interpretation.revision_values: Concrete revisions illustrate a deterministic fixture mutation schedule. Where the contract only requires monotone increments, compare returned current revisions and use them in later requests; do not infer a production DB schema from these counters.
interpretation.durability: Assertions refer to externally observable durable identities/states, not proposed SQL column names. Reopen the isolated store at the specified boundary when these fixtures become executable.
interpretation.public_equality: Compare exact listed keys/types/enums and nulls; no private identity/hash/actor/path/debug field may appear in browser responses. Concrete refusal reasons are fixed in V2. Trusted-import outcome_assertions are harness-level observations because V4 specifies no public import operation/error envelope.
interpretation.claims_vs_paper: transmitted means bytes submitted, not paper accepted. Claim-without-completion stays uncertain even if this harness knows the injected crash preceded bytes.
interpretation.io_counter_scope: All io deltas are per step; arranged prior transport does not count as new sends. Real calls must be zero in every case. fake_payload_calls count payload invocations, never status commands.
interpretation.not_executed: Generation serializes example data and calculates JSON lengths only. Zane must review it before adoption; future implementations must execute the shared fixtures with fake dependencies.
interpretation.reason_selection: For these concrete fixtures, known held content uses content_held and a resolved current-revision ever-claimed child uses invalid_parent, as selected by the engine owner after review. Both well-formed public refusals are durably replayable. Raw malformed trusted import uses invalid_request before issuing a handle. These select existing V4 outcomes; they do not add protocol enums.

common_setup.setup_precedence: Scenario and per-step setup override only explicitly named common fields. Sending examples explicitly open only the simulated applicable gate; never alter a machine setting.
